short: South Korea has a binding comprehensive AI act: the Framework Act on the Development of AI and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust, in force since 22 January 2026, with extraterritorial reach and administrative fines of up to KRW 30 million.
title: South Korea AI Laws
subtitle: The Framework Act on AI, in force since 22 January 2026
body_html:
Status at a glance

Binding comprehensive AI law, in force. South Korea's Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust (인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법) and its Enforcement Decree have applied since 22 January 2026, making Korea the second jurisdiction after the EU with a comprehensive AI statute in force. It reaches foreign businesses whose AI affects Korean users, sets duties for high-impact and generative AI, and requires some foreign operators to appoint a domestic representative. The fines are modest, KRW 30 million at most; the weight of the Act is structural. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Korean national law database.

Reports that the Ministry of Science and ICT will not impose fines for a grace period of at least a year rest on ministry statements in the press. That grace period is not in the Act, the Decree or their supplementary provisions, and this page does not rely on it.

Who regulates and enforces

  • Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT): investigations, stop and corrective orders, and fines (Arts. 40 and 43(2)).
  • National AI Strategy Committee: the presidential committee that sets national AI policy (Art. 7, renamed by Act No. 21311).
  • Personal Information Protection Commission: enforces the Personal Information Protection Act, which governs the personal data AI systems process.

Scope and reach

The Act applies to AI business operators (Art. 2(7)). Under Article 4(1) it applies to acts done abroad if they affect the Korean market or Korean users, so the trigger is where the AI reaches people, not where the company sits. AI used only for national defence or security is excluded (Art. 4(2); Decree Art. 2).

Core obligations

  • Tell users in advance that a high-impact or generative AI product or service is AI-based (Art. 31(1); Decree Art. 23(1)).
  • Label generative AI output, in a form people or machines can read (Art. 31(2); Decree Art. 23(2)), and clearly label realistic synthetic sound, images and video (Art. 31(3)).
  • Safety duties for the largest systems, which must meet all three tests in Decree Article 24: cumulative training compute of 10^26 floating-point operations or more, state of the art, and broad, serious risk to life, safety or rights (Art. 32).
  • Assess in advance whether a system is high-impact, and ask MSIT to confirm where unsure (Art. 33); for high-impact AI, run risk management, explainability, user protection, human oversight and record-keeping (Art. 34); endeavour to assess the impact on fundamental rights (Art. 35, a best-efforts duty).
  • Appoint a domestic representative if the operator has no address in Korea and meets any one of these: prior-year revenue of KRW 1 trillion or more, AI service revenue of KRW 10 billion or more, an average of 1,000,000 or more daily users in Korea over the last three months, or a prior fine under the Act (Art. 36; Decree Art. 29).
  • The binding privacy layer is the Personal Information Protection Act, enforced by the PIPC.

What is coming next

  • 21 April 2027: Act No. 22076 takes effect, adding a training-data integration system (Art. 15-2).
  • Before 1 January 2029: the government must review the compute threshold and the domestic-representative criteria, as it must every three years (Decree Art. 33).
